This is a [[bibliography]] of the Scottish [[comic book writer]] [[Grant Morrison]].

==Comics==
===UK publishers===
Titles published by various British publishers include:
*''[[Near Myths]]'' (script and art, [[anthology]], [[Galaxy Media]]):
** "Time is a Four-Lettered Word" (in #2, 1978)
** "[[Gideon Stargrave|The Vatican Conspiracy]]" (in #3–4, 1978–1979)
** "The Checkmate Man" (in #5, 1980)
*''[[Captain Clyde]]'' (script and art, [[daily comic strip|weekly newspaper strip]], 1979–1982)
** Distributed via three local Scottish newspapers: ''[[Govan|Govan Press]]'', ''[[Renfrew|Renfrew Press]]'' and ''[[Clydebank|Clydebank Press]]''.
** Composed of around 150 episodes published between 1 November 1979 to 5 November 1982.<ref>{{cite web |first= |last= |url=https://globalvariables.net/category/grant-morrison/ |title=Grant Morrison |publisher=globalvariables.net |date=19 January 2019 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200303084042/https://globalvariables.net/category/grant-morrison/ |archivedate=3 March 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*''[[Starblazer]]'' (anthology, [[DC Thomson]]):
** "Algol the Terrible" (script and art, in #15, 1979)
** "Last Man on Earth" (with [[Keith Robson (comics)|Keith Robson]], in #28, 1980)
** "Operation Overkill" (with [[Enrique Alcatena]], in #45, 1981)
** "The Cosmic Outlaw" (with [[José Ortiz (comics)|José Ortiz]], in #86, 1982)
** "The Death Reaper" (with Enrique Alcatena, in #127, 1984)
** "Gateway to Terror" (as inker — on [[Tony O'Donnell (comics)|Tony O'Donnell]]; written by [[N. Austin]], in #142, 1985)
** "Doom World!" (as inker — on Tony O'Donnell; written by [[Ray Aspden (comics)|Ray Aspden]], in #152, 1985)
** "Mind Bender" (with Enrique Alcatena, in #167, 1986)
** "The Midas Mystery" (with Enrique Alcatena, in #177, 1986)
** "The Ring of Gofannon" (with [[Ricardo Garijo]], in #209, 1987)
*''[[Warrior (comics)|Warrior]]'' #26 + ''Spring Special'': "[[The Liberators (comic book)|The Liberators]]" (with [[John Ridgway (comics)|John Ridgway]], anthology, [[Quality Communications]], 1985; 1996)
*''[[Food for Thought (comics)|Food for Thought]]'': "[[Gideon Stargrave|Gideon Stargrave in... Famine]]" (script and art, anthology [[one-shot (comics)|one-shot]], [[Flying Pig Enterprises|Flying Pig]], 1985)
*[[Egmont UK|DC London Editions]]:
**''[[Superman|Superman: Official 1986 Annual]]'': "Osgood Peabody's Big Green Dream Machine..." (three-page prose story with illustrations by [[Barry Kitson]]; 64 pages, 1985, {{ISBN|0-7235-6763-8}})
**''[[Batman|Batman: Official 1986 Annual]]'': "The Stalking" (three-page prose story with illustrations by [[Garry Leach]]; 64 pages, 1985, {{ISBN|0-7235-6762-X}})
*''[[Sunrise (Harrier Comics)|Sunrise]]'' #1–2: "Abraxas: Prologues I and II" (with Tony O'Donnell, co-feature, [[Harrier Comics|Harrier]], 1987)
*''[[Heartbreak Hotel (comics)|Heartbreak Hotel]]'' #4: "Born Again Punk" (script and art, anthology, [[Willyprods/Small Time Ink]], 1988)
*''[[The Adventures of Luther Arkwright]]'' #10 (one-page illustration, [[Valkyrie Press]], 1989)
*''[[Cut (magazine)|Cut]]'' (Jul '89–Sep '89): "[[The New Adventures of Hitler]]" (with [[Steve Yeowell]], strip in the magazine, [[Ideas Ltd]], 1989)
** Three black-and-white six-page installments of this controversial<ref>{{cite web |first=Ben |last=Hansom |url=https://sites.google.com/a/deepspacetransmissions.com/site/news-1/thesavageswordofgrantmorrison-patkanevsthenewadventuresofhitler |title=The Savage Sword of Grant Morrison - Pat Kane vs. The New Adventures of Hitler |publisher=Deep Space Transmissions |date=11 September 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101154803/https://sites.google.com/a/deepspacetransmissions.com/site/news-1/thesavageswordofgrantmorrison-patkanevsthenewadventuresofhitler |archivedate=1 November 2020 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Chris |last=Mautner |url=https://www.cbr.com/collect-this-now-the-new-adventures-of-hitler/ |title=Collect this now! ''The New Adventures of Hitler'' |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]] |date=15 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718103342/http://robot6.comicbookresources.com/2011/07/collect-this-now-the-new-adventures-of-hitler |archive-date=18 July 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Bill |last=Reed |url=http://goodcomics.comicbookresources.com/2007/07/14/365-reasons-to-love-comics-195/ |title=365 Reasons to Love Comics #195 |publisher=Comic Book Resources |date=14 July 2007 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070717202521/http://goodcomics.comicbookresources.com/2007/07/14/365-reasons-to-love-comics-195/ |archivedate=17 July 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref> strip were published before the ''Cut'' magazine ceased publication.
** The colored version of the published chapters as well as the continuation of the story were printed in ''[[Crisis (Fleetway)|Crisis]]'' #46–49 (anthology, [[#Fleetway|Fleetway]], 1990)
*''[[Trident (UK comics)|Trident]]'' #1–4: "[[St. Swithin's Day (comics)|St. Swithin's Day]]" (with [[Paul Grist (comics)|Paul Grist]], anthology, [[Trident Comics|Trident]], 1989–1990)
** A colorized version of the story was published as ''St. Swithin's Day'' (one-shot, Trident, 1990)
** The black-and-white version was published in the US market as ''St. Swithin's Day'' (one-shot, [[Oni Press]], 1998)
*''[[A1 (comic)|A1]]'' #3: "The House of Heart's Desire" (with [[Dom Regan]], anthology, [[Atomeka Press|Atomeka]], 1990)
*''[[Letterbox (book)|Letterbox]]'': "Juliet 4 Romeo" (with Paul Grist, one-page strip in the free giveaway book published by [[Royal Mail]], 1991)
*''[[Così fan tutte|Così Fan Tutte Programme]]'' (untitled four-page strip in programme insert, with [[Cameron Stewart]], [[Scottish Opera]], 2001)
*''[https://web.archive.org/web/20140331094212/http://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-26730067 The Key]'' (with [[Rian Hughes]], a [[webcomic]] commissioned by [[BBC News Online|BBC]] as part of its ''Freedom2014'' initiative, 2014)
** First published in print as a feature in ''[[#Other US publishers|Heavy Metal]]'' #282 (anthology, [[Heavy Metal Media]], 2016)

====Marvel UK====
Titles published by [[Marvel UK]] include:

** "Deserts" (with [[Ron Smith (artist)|Ron Smith]] (#30) and Geoff Senior (#31), in #30–31, 1986)
** "Bits and Pieces" (with John Ridgway, in #36–37, 1986)
** "The Black Zoid" (with [[Kev Hopgood]] and Steve Yeowell (#43, 45–46), in #40–46, 1986–1987)
** "Orientation" (with Steve Yeowell, in #47, 1987)
** "Out of the Blue" (with Steve Yeowell, in #48, 1987)
** "Blue Moon, Red Dawn" (with Steve Yeowell, in #49, 1987)
** "Schumacher's Story" (with [[Phil Gascoine]], in #50, 1987)
*''[[Doctor Who Magazine]]'' (anthology):
**''Doctor Who: The World Shapers'' (tpb, 288 pages, Panini, 2008, {{ISBN|1-905239-87-4}}) includes:
*** "Changes" (with John Ridgway, in #118–119, 1986)
*** "The World Shapers" (with John Ridgway, in #127–129, 1987)
**''Doctor Who: A Cold Day in Hell'' (tpb, 180 pages, Panini, 2009, {{ISBN|1-84653-410-0}}) includes:
*** "Culture Shock" (with [[Bryan Hitch]], in #139, 1988)
*''[[Action Force]]'' (anthology):
**''Action Force'' #17: "[[Shang-Chi|Meditations in Red]]" (with Steve Yeowell, 1987)
**''Action Force Monthly'' #3: "[[Storm Shadow (G.I. Joe)|Old Scores]]" (with [[Mark Farmer (comics)|Mark Farmer]], 1988)

Further short- and long-form prose works include:

*''[[Skin Two]]'' #26: "The Story of Zero" (short story — written to accompany photos by [[Alexander Brattell]] created under the art direction of [[Steven Cook]], 1998)
*''[[Songs of the Black Wurm Gism]]'': "Luvkraft v. Kthulhu" (short story for the book of [[H. P. Lovecraft]] tributes, 356 pages, [[Creation Oneiros Books]], 2009, {{ISBN|1-902197-28-3}})
** The short story is based on a transcript of the spoken word performance staged for the ''Lovecraft Lives'' event (held at [[Waterstone's]] in [[Manchester]] on 6 August 1999)
*''[[Luda (novel)|Luda: A Novel]]'' (448 pages, [[Del Rey Books|Del Rey]], 2022, {{ISBN|0-593-35530-X}})

==Nonfiction and other work==
*''[[ARK (magazine)|ARK]]'' #25–26, 28–29 (short reviews of contemporary comics, [[Titan Magazines|Titan]], 1988–1989)
*''[[Speakeasy (magazine)|Speakeasy]]'' #101–119: "Drivel" (opinion column in the comics magazine, [[John Brown Publishing]], 1989–1991)
** A one-off installment titled "Son of Drivel: From My Pulpit" was published in ''[[Tripwire (magazine)|Tripwire]]'' #3 ([[Tripwire Publishing|Tripwire]], 1992)
*''[[Rapid Eye (book)|Rapid Eye]] Volume 3'': "[[Maya Deren|In Search of Maya Deren]]" (biographical piece for the book of essays, 256 pages, [[Creation Books]], 1995, {{ISBN|1-871592-24-0}})
*''[[Sleazenation]]'': "The Smell of Reason" (irregular column — only three (heavily edited)<ref>{{cite web |first=Warren |last=Ellis |url=http://www.comicbookresources.com/columns/index.cgi?column=cia&article=492 |title=Come In Alone: Issue #128 |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]] |date=9 June 2000 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20010411025532/http://www.comicbookresources.com/columns/index.cgi?column=cia&article=492 |archivedate=11 April 2001 |quote=The SLEAZE NATION column was something I'd love to have done regularly but they kept inexplicably editing out my best stuff without telling me, so I stopped. |url-status=dead }}</ref> installments were published, [[Swinstead Publishing]], 1998–2000)<ref>{{cite web |first=Grant |last=Morrison |url=http://grantmorrison.com/SOR1.htm |title=the smell of reason 1 - heil photo sapiens! 1998 |publisher=grantmorrison.com |date= |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20020411032744/http://grantmorrison.com/SOR1.htm |archivedate=11 April 2002 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Grant |last=Morrison |url=http://grantmorrison.com/SOR2.htm |title=the smell of reason 2: two breasts for britain! 1998 |publisher=grantmorrison.com |date= |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20020605012726/http://www.grantmorrison.com/SOR2.htm |archivedate=5 June 2002 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Grant |last=Morrison |url=http://grantmorrison.com/SOR3.htm |title=the smell of reason 3 : viva le fear! 2000 |publisher=grantmorrison.com |date= |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20020605012152/http://www.grantmorrison.com/SOR3.htm |archivedate=5 June 2002 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*''[[Malaparte: A House Like Me]]'': "Unbuilding Malaparte" (short prose piece for the book about [[Casa Malaparte]], 200 pages, [[Crown Publishing Group|Clarkson Potter]], 2000, {{ISBN|0-609-60378-7}})
*''[[Fortune Hotel]]'': "It was the 90s" (short piece detailing Morrison's [[Grant Morrison#1990s|Kathmandu experience]] for the book of travelogues, 320 pages, [[Penguin Books|Penguin]], 2000, {{ISBN|0-14-028108-8}})
*''[https://web.archive.org/web/20060218180126/http://www.grantmorrison.com/column_archive1.htm Come Ride My Column]'' (irregular column published via an older version of Morrison's website, 2000–2002)
*''[[Book of Lies: The Disinformation Guide to Magick and the Occult]]'': "Pop Magic!" (essay for the magic-themed book, 352 pages, [[Disinfo]], 2003, {{ISBN|0-9713942-7-X}})
** A revised and expanded version of this essay was published under the title "Beyond the World and the Fool" in ''[[Heavy Metal (magazine)|Heavy Metal]]'' #286 ([[Heavy Metal Media]], 2017)
*''[[Supergods]]'' (part autobiography, part analysis of the history of superheroes) published under two different subtitles:
** Published in the UK, EU and Commonwealth countries (excluding Canada) by [[Jonathan Cape]] as ''Supergods: Our World in the Age of the Superhero'' (hc, 480 pages, 2011, {{ISBN|0-224-08996-X}}; sc, 2012, {{ISBN|0-09-954667-1}})
** Published in the US by [[Spiegel & Grau]] as ''Supergods: What Masked Vigilantes, Miraculous Mutants, and a Sun God from Smallville Can Teach Us About Being Human'' (hc, 480 pages, 2011, {{ISBN|1-4000-6912-2}}; sc, 2012, {{ISBN|0-8129-8138-3}})
*''[[Heavy Metal (magazine)|Heavy Metal]]'' #280–285, 287–292 ([[editorial]]s in the comics magazine, Heavy Metal Media, 2016–2018)
*''[https://grantmorrison.substack.com/ Xanaduum: The Project of a Lifetime]'' (newsletter published via [[Substack]], 2022–present)
